finding.claim: Unauthenticated /fetch handler passes the attacker-supplied 'target' query parameter straight to http.Get and streams the full response body back to the client, giving full-read SSRF to any http/https destination reachable from the server, including internal hosts and cloud metadata (169.254.169.254).
finding.sink: main.go:16 http.Get(target); response body reflected via main.go:22 io.Copy(w, resp.Body)

trace.note: /fetch is registered on the default mux with no auth or middleware
target read directly from the query string, no parsing or normalization
http.Get(target) performs the outbound request with the unvalidated URL
on error, err.Error() is returned to the client, so connection errors (e.g. 'dial tcp 10.x.x.x:port: connection refused') act as an error-based port-scan oracle
upstream response body is copied to the client, so the response is fully readable by the attacker

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. No hostname/IP allowlist, no scheme check, no auth, no size or timeout limit. Mitigating factor: Go's default transport rejects non-http(s) schemes, so file:// and gopher:// are not reachable. http and https to any host or IP are reachable, and redirects are followed.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /fetch path (main.go:14-23) has no hostname check, scheme check, or auth. The allowlist at main.go:9-12 and the hostname check at main.go:27 belong only to safeFetch, which is registered on a separate route (main.go:42) and is not on the /fetch path.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled `target` query parameter (main.go:15) goes straight into http.Get (main.go:16) with no validation, and the response body is copied back to the client (main.go:22), while /fetch is registered unauthenticated on the default mux (main.go:41); the allowlist that exists in safeFetch (main.go:27) does not apply to this route.

finding.claim: The /safe handler validates only the original URL's hostname against an exact-match allowlist, then calls http.Get with default redirect-following. An allowed host that responds with a redirect to an internal or metadata address is followed without re-validation, bypassing the allowlist. The response is also reflected to the client.
finding.sink: main.go:31 http.Get(u.String()) using the default client, which follows up to 10 redirects with no CheckRedirect hook; response reflected via main.go:37 io.Copy(w, resp.Body)

trace.note: /safe is registered on the default mux
validation: err == nil and u.Hostname() must be an exact key in allowed (images.example.org, docs.example.org)
http.Get(u.String()) re-serializes the parsed URL and fetches it with the default client, which follows redirects
the allowlist is never re-applied to any Location target
final response body is copied to the client

finding.guards_checked: Parser differential: validator and fetcher both use net/url, and the fetcher uses u.String(), so userinfo tricks (allowed.org@evil, allowed.org\@evil, allowed.org#@evil) were checked and fail the Hostname() check or still resolve to an allowed host. Scheme: Go's client rejects non-http(s) schemes. Port is not checked, but a port does not change the host. Not guarded: redirect following, which has no per-hop re-validation. DNS resolution happens at fetch time with no resolved-IP check. The exploit needs an allowed host to redirect (open redirect or user content on images/docs.example.org) or to resolve to an internal IP (DNS takeover), so it is conditional. Verdict: plausible, conditional on control of an allowed host.

verdict.guard_found: main.go:27 exact-match hostname check (allowed[u.Hostname()]) on the original URL only. No re-validation of redirect targets: http.Get at main.go:31 uses the default client, which follows redirects with no CheckRedirect, and nothing between lines 31 and 37 checks the final host.
verdict.reason: The source is the attacker-controlled target query parameter (main.go:26), and the allowlist at main.go:27 applies only to the first URL, so the default redirect-following http.Get at main.go:31 can reach an internal or metadata address via a redirect from an allowed host, with the body reflected at main.go:37. The exploit still requires an allowed host that redirects (open redirect or user-controlled content), which is outside this code, but the code itself has no closing guard for that path.
